title: Alibaba’s Qwen3.8-Max Launch: What BABA vs. BIDU Means for Investors

content_html:
Alibaba (NYSE:BABA) unveiled its largest and most capable AI model to date on August 3, and the market noticed immediately, sending its Hong Kong-listed shares up about 7% the same day. The new model, Qwen3.8-Max, arrives as Chinese AI developers race each other on a near-weekly cadence, and it is another data point in the case that Alibaba is becoming an AI infrastructure company that still gets priced like an e-commerce one.

The Bull Case: A Frontier Model With A Cloud Payoff

Qwen3.8-Max is built on 2.4 trillion parameters and uses a mixture-of-experts design that activates only about 95 billion of them at a time, cutting compute costs and response delays. In internal testing, it independently executed a software engineering project over 16 days, and on chatbot arena leaderboards it ranked fifth in Text Arena and second on Vision Arena. Alibaba plans to release the model's weights for public download next week.

That open-weight approach is the point. Alibaba does not need Qwen itself to generate revenue directly. Every developer who builds on it needs computing power, hosting, storage and other infrastructure, and that demand flows straight into Alibaba Cloud. The timing lines up with what the cloud unit has already been doing: Alibaba's Cloud Intelligence Group reported total fourth-quarter revenue of RMB 41.63 billion (up 38% YoY) and accelerated external revenue growth to 40% in Q4 FY2026, while AI-related product revenue has posted triple-digit growth for 11 straight quarters.

The Bear Case: A Crowded, Undiscounted Race

Alibaba is not winning this race by a wide margin. Qwen3.8-Max's 2.4 trillion parameters still trail Moonshot's Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion parameter model that rattled global stock markets and Silicon Valley when it launched last month. DeepSeek added more pressure on Friday with its V4-Flash model, priced at just $0.14 per million input tokens, a fraction of what larger models charge and, according to Artificial Analysis, cheaper on a per-task basis than Kimi K3, GPT-5.6 Sol or Claude Fable 5. Giving away frontier models for free only pays off if enough of that traffic converts into paid cloud usage, and that conversion is still a bet, not a result.

Alibaba's core commerce business adds its own drag. Domestic growth has decelerated as Pinduoduo, JD.com and Douyin compete harder, and a quick-commerce price war raises real questions about near-term profitability. The AI buildout itself is expensive, and Alibaba still needs both to keep spending on models and cloud infrastructure and to stabilize a retail business that generates most of its revenue today.

content_html_zh:
阿里巴巴（纽约证券交易所股票代码：BABA）于 8 月 3 日推出了迄今为止规模最大、能力最强的人工智能模型，立即引起市场关注，当天其在香港上市的股价上涨约 7%。 新型号 Qwen3.8-Max 的出现正值中国人工智能开发者以近乎每周一次的节奏相互竞争之际，这是阿里巴巴正在成为一家人工智能基础设施公司但定价仍像电子商务公司那样的另一个数据点。

牛市案例：具有云回报的前沿模型

Qwen3.8-Max 基于 2.4 万亿个参数构建，并采用专家混合设计，一次仅激活约 950 亿个参数，从而降低了计算成本和响应延迟。 在内部测试中，它独立执行了一个软件工程项目超过16天，在聊天机器人竞技场排行榜上，它在Text Arena排名第五，在Vision Arena排名第二。 阿里巴巴计划下周发布该模型的权重供公众下载。

这种开放重量的方法才是重点。 阿里巴巴并不需要Qwen本身来直接产生收入。 每个在其上构建的开发人员都需要计算能力、托管、存储和其他基础设施，而这种需求直接流入阿里云。 这一时机与云部门已经采取的行动一致：阿里巴巴云智能集团报告第四季度总收入为人民币 416.3 亿元（同比增长 38%），并在 2026 财年第四季度将外部收入增长加速至 40%，而人工智能相关产品收入连续 11 个季度实现三位数增长。

熊市：一场拥挤的、不打折的比赛

阿里巴巴并未以大幅优势赢得这场竞赛。 Qwen3.8-Max 的 2.4 万亿参数仍然落后于 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3，后者是上个月推出时震惊全球股市和硅谷的 2.8 万亿参数模型。 DeepSeek 周五推出的 V4-Flash 模型增加了更大的压力，每百万输入代币的价格仅为 0.14 美元，只是较大模型收费的一小部分，而且根据 Artificial Analysis 的数据，按每个任务计算，它比 Kimi K3、GPT-5.6 Sol 或 Claude Fable 5 更便宜。 只有当足够的流量转化为付费云使用时，免费赠送前沿模型才会有回报，而且这种转化仍然是一种赌注，而不是结果。

阿里巴巴的核心商业业务也增加了自身的拖累。 随着拼多多、京东和抖音的竞争更加激烈，国内增长已经放缓，而快速的商业价格战引发了人们对近期盈利能力的真正质疑。 人工智能建设本身成本高昂，阿里巴巴仍然需要继续在模型和云基础设施上投入资金，并稳定目前产生大部分收入的零售业务。
